title: Declare the train family that matches its terminal contract

facts.note: Planner work that authors, edits, reviews or validates train definitions.

Any train definition is in scope, whether newly authored, edited for any reason, or already existing and merely being checked; the constraint is a standing validity invariant, not edit-scoped. The family/terminal comparison itself is the obligation's content; its validator binding is pending (D1, #1085) and is recorded in verifier_detail/audit, not used as an activation claim.

fires: A train's terminal requires an Acceptance Authority commit and its terminal primary is platform:acceptance:commit-receipt, but family is declared as behavior.
A train is declared family:delivery while its terminal does not require an Acceptance Authority commit, or its terminal primary is something other than platform:acceptance:commit-receipt.
A train definition has no family field at all.
An existing, untouched train definition encountered during planning or validation already has a family that disagrees with its terminal contract, or lacks a family field.
doesNotFire: A train with an Acceptance Authority commit terminal whose primary is platform:acceptance:commit-receipt, declared family:delivery.
A train whose terminal does not satisfy both delivery conditions, declared family:behavior.
Planning artifacts that are not train definitions (wagons, WMBTs, acceptances, docs) with no family/terminal fields.

given: A train definition (new, edited or existing) declares a terminal contract
when: the planner authors, edits, reviews or validates that train definition
then: Ensure the train declares family:delivery if and only if the terminal requires an Acceptance Authority commit AND the terminal primary is platform:acceptance:commit-receipt, and family:behavior otherwise.
prefer: Decide the terminal contract first, then derive the family from it; the family is controlled redundancy that mirrors the terminal contract.
When editing a terminal contract, update the family in the same change so the two stay consistent.
avoid: Omitting the family field — a missing family is invalid, not a default.
Declaring family:delivery when only one of the two conditions holds (Acceptance Authority commit required, primary = platform:acceptance:commit-receipt).
Treating the family as a second source of truth that overrides or diverges from the terminal contract.
why: The family is fixed by the terminal contract; keeping it as checked, controlled redundancy (not an independent source of truth) prevents trains being routed or validated under the wrong family.
evidence: Each train definition has a family field present.
family is delivery exactly when terminal requires an Acceptance Authority commit and terminal primary == platform:acceptance:commit-receipt; behavior in every other case.
Validator conventions/coherence/test_train_family_matches_terminal_contract::test_fault_injection passes (binding pending — validator owned by D1, #1085).
verifier_detail: Biconditional check over every train definition (not only changed ones): expected_family = 'delivery' if (terminal.requires_acceptance_authority_commit AND terminal.primary == 'platform:acceptance:commit-receipt') else 'behavior'; finding when declared family != expected_family.
Missing family field is itself a finding (invalid), regardless of terminal contract.
Term family_consistency (label 'Family consistency'): declared family <-> declared terminal contract; controlled redundancy, not a second source of truth.
Pending binding - validator owned by D1 (#1085). Implementation type validator, ref conventions/coherence/test_train_family_matches_terminal_contract::test_fault_injection.
audit: Pending binding - validator owned by D1 (#1085).
